paragraphs: The paper studies how to learn population dynamics from snapshots of distributions over time. These snapshots describe where a population is at particular moments, while the forces driving its movement remain unknown. A common modeling approach uses Wasserstein gradient flows, which describe motion through decreasing free energy. The authors argue that this perspective misses important behaviors, including periodic motion.

They instead formulate population dynamics through a principle of least Lagrangian action. From this principle, they derive Hamiltonian equations describing population motion. Their theoretical framework encompasses classical mechanics, quantum mechanics, and gradient flows, placing these forms of dynamics within a shared mathematical description.

The Hamiltonian formulation also supports an algorithm that learns mechanics from observed distributions without requiring a specified Lagrangian or a reference process. In real and simulated experiments, the method predicts future distributions and fills gaps between observations, outperforming gradient flow and flow matching methods. The findings support learning richer population mechanics directly from snapshots.
icml-2026-a-call-to-lagrangian-action-le.tldr: A population-level action principle enables learning richer dynamics from distribution snapshots, including behaviors that gradient flows cannot capture.

paragraphs: ASRU addresses the problem of removing sensitive knowledge from models that process multiple modalities while keeping their responses useful. The authors argue that judging unlearning mainly by changes in model outputs can overlook response quality. A model might stop producing the targeted information yet respond with hallucinations or inflexible refusals, undermining the usefulness of the unlearning procedure.

The framework makes generation quality an explicit objective. It first redirects internal activations to induce refusal behavior. It then uses reinforcement learning with a customized reward to refine the boundary between requests that should be refused and those the model should still handle. These stages connect an initial behavioral change with more selective control over that behavior.

Experiments on Qwen3-VL report average improvements of 24.6% in unlearning effectiveness and 5.8 times in generation quality while preserving model utility. The method uses only a small amount of retained supervision data. The results support evaluating unlearning through both targeted forgetting and the quality of the model that remains.
icml-2026-asru-activation-steering-meets.tldr: ASRU combines activation steering and reinforcement learning to improve targeted multimodal unlearning while preserving useful, higher-quality responses.

paragraphs: CAD generation often treats a design program as a sequence of tokens describing operations and their arguments. The difficulty is that producing plausible tokens does not itself establish a clear connection to the resulting geometry. Existing approaches can supply visual inputs or render completed programs, but the authors identify a gap in feedback about the geometric effects of individual intermediate tokens.

Their Argument-induced 3D Point Loss maps argument tokens to corresponding points in three-dimensional space. This gives training a geometric signal at the token level, connecting program arguments with their spatial consequences. A complementary Grammar-constrained Operator uses CAD program structure to regulate generation, with the aim of simplifying learning and reducing invalid sequences.

The authors evaluate the approach on five CAD generation tasks with inputs including text, SVG sketches, point clouds, and CAD sequences. They report improved generation accuracy and program validity across input modalities. Together, the two components address whether a generated program follows valid structure and whether its arguments produce the intended geometry.
icml-2026-bridging-tokens-and-geometry-t.tldr: Token-level geometric supervision and grammar-constrained generation improve the accuracy and validity of CAD programs across different input modalities.

paragraphs: This paper explores storing visual content through adaptations to a pretrained generative model. Its starting observation is that generative models already contain extensive visual knowledge, but conventional representations such as pixels, tokens, and latent arrays remain separate from that knowledge. The authors seek a representation that makes the model's learned generation process part of how the content is encoded.

They represent a visual signal as a function parameterized by low-rank adaptations attached to a frozen generative model. These adaptations provide the signal-specific representation while the underlying model stays fixed. The resulting implicit representation can also be hashed into a compact vector; the abstract gives an 81-frame video as an example of content represented this way.

The authors report strong perceptual video compression at extremely low bitrates. Because decoding involves a function within the generation process, additional inference-time computation and control can further refine compression performance. This connection suggests a broader framework joining compression and generation, with the pretrained model's visual knowledge contributing directly to representation and reconstruction.
icml-2026-compression-as-adaptation-impl.tldr: Visual content can be encoded as small adaptations to a frozen generative model, supporting compact storage and inference-time refinement.

paragraphs: The paper addresses uncertainty estimates for forecasts of multiple time series linked by a graph. Conformal prediction offers coverage guarantees under exchangeability, meaning that permuting observations leaves their joint distribution unchanged. Relationships among graph nodes can violate this condition, making a direct application of conformal prediction unreliable even when point forecasts are useful.

The authors use graph spectral structure to separate global trends from higher-frequency variation. Their premise is that cross-node coupling appears in low-frequency components, while high-frequency components are nearly exchangeable. They introduce Spectral Graph Conditional Exchangeability, which conditions the high-frequency components on the low-frequency ones so that global trends remain represented.

Their SCALE method implements this idea using graph wavelets. It calibrates high-frequency prediction residuals through adaptive gating informed by a low-frequency embedding. Across real-world benchmarks from multiple domains, SCALE achieves valid coverage and improves the trade-off between coverage and efficiency over the compared conformal methods. These empirical findings support accounting for graph dependence explicitly when constructing forecast uncertainty.
icml-2026-delving-into-non-exchangeabili.tldr: SCALE separates graph-linked time series into spectral components to improve conformal uncertainty estimates while accounting for shared trends.

paragraphs: Long reasoning traces make reasoning models expensive because inference retains information about earlier tokens for subsequent computation. This paper examines attention maps and finds that some tokens play a much larger role in steering the final answer than others. In the authors' analysis, many remaining reasoning tokens contribute negligibly to that decision.

Dynamic Thinking-Token Selection, or DynTS, uses this observation to manage the key-value cache. It identifies decision-critical tokens and keeps their cached states, while removing entries associated with redundant tokens. The intervention targets the retained inference state: the method allocates limited cache capacity according to which parts of the reasoning trace matter for reaching the answer.

Across six benchmarks, DynTS improves Pass@1 by 2.6% over state-of-the-art cache compression methods at the same budget. Compared with vanilla Transformers, it reports inference speedups of 1.84–2.62 times and reductions in peak cache memory of 3.32–5.73 times without compromising reasoning performance. These findings support selective retention as a practical route to more efficient reasoning inference.
icml-2026-dynamic-thinking-token-selecti.tldr: DynTS retains cached states for decision-critical reasoning tokens, reducing inference time and memory while preserving reported reasoning performance.

paragraphs: An LLM serving system can produce worse answers without crashing or emitting an explicit error. Such silent failures are difficult to diagnose because a visible symptom in language quality can originate deep within an optimized software stack. Ekka addresses the task of connecting these high-level symptoms to the underlying implementation faults.

The system treats diagnosis as differential debugging, using a semantically correct implementation as a reference. It systematically aligns intermediate execution states between the reference and the target serving framework, then compares them to identify root causes. This provides evidence inside the computation rather than relying solely on the final generated answer. The approach depends on the availability of an appropriate correct reference.

The authors construct a benchmark from real silent errors in popular serving frameworks. Ekka achieves 80% diagnosis accuracy at pass@1 and 88% at pass@5, outperforming the compared state-of-the-art systems. It also diagnoses four previously unknown silent errors confirmed by developers, showing usefulness beyond reproducing diagnoses for the benchmark's existing cases.
icml-2026-ekka-automated-diagnosis-of-si.tldr: Ekka diagnoses silent LLM serving errors by comparing intermediate execution states with a correct reference implementation.

paragraphs: Remote sensing institutions hold large collections of unlabeled data with multiple views of the same underlying environments. Combining these collections centrally can create communication costs and privacy concerns. This paper proposes a federated clustering framework that coordinates learning across institutions while exchanging privatized cluster prototypes masked with adaptive noise instead of sensitive data features.

The framework first uses superpixel segmentation to reduce spatial dimensionality and computational work. It then addresses a coordination problem: different institutions can assign inconsistent cluster identities. A co-occurrence structural alignment module synchronizes their local models so that their clustering results can contribute to a more consistent shared representation.

A further component uses Wasserstein prototype contrastive learning to represent clusters as distributions rather than individual points. This is intended to improve global consistency and robustness when institutions have heterogeneous data. Experiments on four public datasets report better clustering performance and efficiency than the compared state-of-the-art methods. The combined design tackles local computation, communication, and agreement among distributed clustering models.
icml-2026-federated-multi-view-clusterin.tldr: A federated clustering framework shares noise-masked prototypes and aligns local clusters to improve remote sensing analysis across institutions.

paragraphs: Neural tangent kernels provide a mathematical way to study neural network training. They become especially tractable when network width is taken to infinity, but that limit omits effects such as feature learning and changes in the kernel during training. This paper develops tools for calculating corrections that bring finite network width back into the analysis.

The authors introduce Feynman diagrams to simplify the algebra needed for these corrections. Their framework yields layer-by-layer recursions for statistics involving preactivations, neural tangent kernels, and higher-derivative tensors used to predict leading-order training dynamics. The contribution is a systematic computational language for quantities that otherwise require complicated manipulations.

They extend deep-network stability results to neural tangent kernels and prove that finite-width corrections vanish on the kernel Gram matrix diagonal for scale-invariant nonlinearities such as ReLU. This statement concerns those diagonal entries. Numerical first-order corrections for arbitrary inputs follow sampled-network statistics at widths around 20 and above, demonstrating the framework's empirical feasibility in the tested setting.
icml-2026-finite-width-neural-tangent-ke.tldr: Feynman diagrams simplify finite-width corrections to neural tangent kernels, enabling theoretical and numerical analysis beyond infinite-width networks.

paragraphs: This paper represents a long video's semantic content in a small set of network weights attached to a vision-language model. The resulting Neural Knowledge Representation becomes a reusable asset for answering questions about that video. Its purpose is to avoid repeatedly loading or encoding the original video when users ask multiple questions.

Creating this representation requires a one-time Agentic Knowledge Distillation phase. An agent synthesizes detailed descriptions and question-answer pairs, which are used to optimize the video-specific weights. At inference, those weights are attached to a frozen vision-language model, allowing it to answer queries using the distilled content.

The approach separates the cost of preparing video knowledge from the cost of later interactions. Its efficiency advantage is therefore especially relevant when the representation is reused across turns. On LVBench, the authors report performance comparable to state-of-the-art approaches and an end-to-end latency reduction exceeding two orders of magnitude. The findings support storing reusable semantic knowledge in model weights for interactive long-video understanding.
icml-2026-from-content-to-knowledge-ligh.tldr: A one-time distillation process stores video knowledge in small reusable network weights, enabling fast follow-up queries without re-encoding the video.

paragraphs: LIMMT examines how the choice of motion training data affects physics-based humanoid motion tracking. The authors argue that high-quality examples can guide a tracking policy toward better optimization trajectories early in training. This shifts attention toward the composition of the training set and how those examples influence the learning process.

Their definition of quality goes beyond identifying and deleting erroneous clips. It includes three dimensions: physical feasibility, diversity, and complexity. These dimensions distinguish whether motions are compatible with physics, how varied the selected motions are, and how complex they are. The framework treats data selection as a substantive part of learning a capable tracking policy.

The central reported finding is that training on less than 3% of AMASS produces better tracking performance than training on the complete dataset. Additional experiments and analyses support the framework's effectiveness. This result shows that, in the evaluated setting, a carefully chosen small training collection can be more useful than the full available motion dataset.
icml-2026-limmt-less-is-more-for-motion-.tldr: LIMMT improves humanoid motion tracking by selecting training data for physical feasibility, diversity, and complexity, using less than 3% of AMASS.

paragraphs: MASH trains language models to seek help selectively and uses that behavior to infer when they should abstain from answering from internal knowledge. The motivating problem is that models often fail to recognize their knowledge boundaries and produce unsupported answers. The authors propose that a decision to search can become a useful signal of those boundaries.

The framework uses reinforcement learning that rewards accurate answers while charging a penalty for each search. This creates an incentive to use external help when it contributes enough to answering correctly. The claim is conditional on this reward design: appropriately penalized help-seeking can serve as a proxy for abstention.

Across three knowledge-intensive question-answering datasets, MASH improves selective help-seeking over prior efficient search approaches, including a reported 7.6% accuracy improvement on multi-hop datasets. Its abstention behavior is also competitive with methods that require advance identification of knowledge boundaries to construct training data. The findings connect efficient tool use and abstention through a shared learned decision about when internal knowledge is sufficient.
icml-2026-mash-modeling-abstention-via-s.tldr: MASH rewards answer accuracy while penalizing searches, making selective help-seeking useful for both efficient retrieval and abstention.

paragraphs: MOC studies how messages move through systems of collaborating language-model agents. Many existing approaches concatenate responses from immediate neighbors. The authors argue that this restricts which evidence an agent receives and allows important insights to become diluted as messages travel through multiple agents. Their focus is the information transmitted over the communication structure.

The proposed Multi-Order Communication scheme constructs a structured evidence stream that captures dependencies across multiple communication hops. It also consolidates messages to control their size. A Semantic-Topological Merging algorithm combines attention to message meaning with information about communication structure, seeking to preserve semantic fidelity within a limited token budget.

Experiments cover six datasets and language-model backbones of different parameter scales. MOC consistently improves task performance while reducing communication costs in these evaluations. The result indicates that giving agents access to better-organized evidence can improve collaboration without requiring larger message volumes. Its contribution joins broader access to multi-hop information with a concrete method for keeping that information compact.
icml-2026-moc-multi-order-communication-.tldr: MOC organizes and merges evidence across multiple agent communication hops, improving task performance while reducing communication costs.

paragraphs: This paper asks how reliably a monitor can detect problematic agent behavior from a model's chain of thought. It treats monitorability as a property to measure because changes in training, data, or scale may affect it. The authors introduce intervention, process, and outcome-property evaluation archetypes, alongside a metric and broad evaluation suite.

Their evaluations find that inspecting chain of thought outperforms monitoring actions alone in practical settings. Frontier models are generally monitorable, though imperfectly, and longer reasoning traces are typically easier to monitor. At a fixed capability level, a smaller model using more reasoning effort can provide greater monitorability, with a corresponding increase in inference computation.

The monitor's own resources also matter. Giving a weak monitor more test-time computation improves its monitoring of a stronger agent. Access to the agent's reasoning improves both monitorability and how it scales with compute. Follow-up questions provide another route: sharing the resulting follow-up reasoning with the monitor improves detection visibility. These findings identify several empirical ways to strengthen oversight.
icml-2026-monitoring-monitorability-6cbf.tldr: A new evaluation suite finds that reasoning access, additional compute, and follow-up questions can improve agent monitorability, though monitoring remains imperfect.

paragraphs: MutAtlas addresses the scarcity of experimentally measured protein mutation effects by building a large supplementary dataset. It enumerates single-site substitutions on experimentally resolved protein structures across the PDB and aligns signals from physics-based energy models, protein language models, and inverse folding models. These sources provide different perspectives on which mutations are preferred.

A unified representation lets the authors compare those preferences directly. They find substantial differences in agreement, concentration, and substitution patterns across models. Their analysis interprets this disagreement as pervasive and connected to conflicting modeling biases, rather than simply random noise. That finding motivates a learning method that explicitly represents disagreement between sources.

The resulting unsupervised distillation framework learns relative mutation preferences without experimental mutation labels during training. On ProteinGym, it achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated zero-shot baselines and naive multi-source fusion strategies. The result supports combining sources while accounting for their conflicts. The released dataset and evaluation pipeline also provide a basis for reproducible mutation-effect research.
icml-2026-mutatlas-a-pdb-wide-energy-gui.tldr: MutAtlas combines large-scale mutation signals through unsupervised distillation that explicitly models disagreement among protein prediction methods.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether automated advertising bidders benefit from coordinating their participation in auctions. It considers bidders managed by a shared third-party agent and multiple campaigns controlled by one advertiser. These settings create a common coordination question: how should participants choose bids when their aggregate value and spending compliance matter?

The authors formalize a mechanism in which only the coordinated bidder with the highest value competes against outside bidders. Other members of the coordinated group refrain from competing. Their theoretical analysis shows that this mechanism dominates independent bidding for a broad class of auto-bidding algorithms, improving both total accrued value and Return-on-Spend compliance.

Simulations using synthetic and real-world datasets support the theoretical advantage. The findings indicate that coordination can improve outcomes for participating bidders or campaigns under the studied model and algorithms. The contribution connects a simple participation rule with both mathematical analysis and empirical support, showing how the decision about which coordinated bidder enters can affect the group's overall auction outcomes.
icml-2026-on-the-coordination-of-value-m.tldr: Allowing only the highest-value coordinated bidder to compete improves group value and Return-on-Spend compliance for a broad class of auto-bidding algorithms.

paragraphs: PathWise uses collaborating language-model agents to design heuristics for combinatorial optimization. The authors identify a problem with systems built around fixed evolutionary rules and static prompts: they can generate candidates myopically, repeat evaluations, and make limited use of the reasoning behind earlier derivations. PathWise makes the evolving search history part of the decision process.

It represents heuristic generation as sequential decision-making over an entailment graph that stores a compact, persistent account of the search trajectory. A policy agent plans evolutionary actions, while a world-model agent generates heuristic rollouts conditioned on those actions. Critic agents supply routed reflections that summarize lessons from earlier steps.

This organization lets later generations reuse useful derivation information and avoid paths informed by previous experience. Across diverse combinatorial optimization problems, the authors report faster convergence to better heuristics, generalization across language-model backbones, and scaling to larger problem sizes. The findings support explicit memory and planning as useful components of automated heuristic design, connecting candidate generation with the accumulated reasoning of the search.
icml-2026-pathwise-planning-through-worl.tldr: PathWise coordinates planning, generation, and critique agents around a persistent search graph to develop better optimization heuristics faster.

paragraphs: PolicyGuard addresses backdoors in reinforcement-learning agents. A compromised agent may behave normally until a particular trigger causes malicious actions, making the moment of activation an important detection target. The authors note that existing defenses can require internal model parameters, assess entire models or trajectories, or cover only particular kinds of attacks.

Their method operates during testing and assesses individual time steps. It uses Gaussian-process posterior variance as an uncertainty signal and adapts pseudo trajectories so that uncertainty can be computed at this finer resolution. The paper also develops theoretical foundations explaining why this variance signal is useful for the proposed defense.

Experiments across seven reinforcement-learning games show state-of-the-art detection performance in most evaluated cases. Average AUROC is 0.856 for perturbation-based attacks and 0.859 for adversary-agent attacks. These results support the usefulness of uncertainty-based detection at the step level across the two evaluated attack categories. The contribution is a test-time detection method whose decisions can be associated with individual moments in an agent's behavior.
icml-2026-policyguard-towards-test-time-.tldr: PolicyGuard uses Gaussian-process uncertainty to detect backdoor-triggered behavior at individual reinforcement-learning time steps during testing.

paragraphs: The paper improves tests of Granger non-causality for panel data, where multiple units are observed over time and their behavior may differ. Its focus is statistical power: the ability of a test to detect departures from non-causality when such signals are present. This becomes challenging in large panels, particularly when meaningful signals occur in only a few units.

The proposed PE-PGCT adds a power-enhancement component to an existing panel Granger non-causality test. The authors establish asymptotic guarantees showing that this component produces negligible distortion of the test's size under the null while increasing power under alternatives. In practical terms, the enhancement aims to improve detection without materially changing the false-positive behavior in the theoretical limit.

Theoretical and empirical findings show especially substantial gains when there are more panel units than time observations, and when signals are sparse across units. Extensive simulations and a real-world application illustrate performance. The contribution is an enhancement usable with existing panel tests, with benefits concentrated in statistically difficult high-dimensional and sparse settings.
icml-2026-power-boosted-granger-causal-d.tldr: PE-PGCT enhances existing panel Granger tests, especially for high-dimensional or sparse signals, with asymptotically negligible null size distortion.

paragraphs: CoSMo addresses the computational expense of long reasoning chains by changing their structure. The authors focus on redundancy between reasoning segments and gaps in the logic connecting them. Their goal is to preserve coherent problem-solving while reducing unnecessary reasoning structure, so efficiency depends on how the chain is organized.

A consistency-guided split-merge algorithm performs two complementary operations. It merges segments that repeat reasoning and splits segments where logical gaps need attention. The framework then applies structure-aligned reinforcement learning with a segment-level budget, training the model to maintain efficient reasoning organization. This couples an explicit restructuring procedure with a learning objective that reinforces the desired structure.

Across multiple benchmarks and model backbones, CoSMo improves accuracy by 3.3 points and reduces segment usage by 28.7% on average relative to reasoning-efficiency baselines. These results show that fewer reasoning segments can coexist with stronger answers in the evaluated settings. The reported savings concern segment usage, while the central contribution is a training framework for removing redundancy without abandoning logical coherence.
icml-2026-short-chains-deep-thoughts-bal.tldr: CoSMo restructures reasoning through consistency-guided splitting and merging, improving accuracy while reducing the number of reasoning segments.

paragraphs: SIGMA-PPG develops a foundation model for photoplethysmography signals, addressing the redundancy and noise that complicate representation learning. The authors argue that ordinary masked modeling can admit trivial solutions, while contrastive approaches can fail to preserve precise waveform shape. Their method combines challenging reconstruction tasks with constraints on the consistency of learned representations.

A reinforcement-learning teacher uses statistical priors to choose adversarial masks and create challenging learning paths. This mechanism is intended to prevent the model from overfitting to noise. A second component uses vector quantization to assign physiologically identical waveforms to shared codebook indices, including when recording artifacts or small perturbations alter their appearance.

Together, these mechanisms encourage informative learning tasks and compact representations that retain physiological meaning. The model is pretrained on more than 120,000 hours of data and achieves better average performance than five state-of-the-art baselines across 12 downstream tasks. The findings support combining prior-guided masking with semantic consistency to improve reusable PPG representations across a diverse set of evaluated applications.
icml-2026-sigma-ppg-statistical-prior-in.tldr: SIGMA-PPG combines statistically guided adversarial masking and consistent waveform codes to improve PPG representations across downstream tasks.

paragraphs: TimeOmni-VL seeks to combine understanding time series with generating accurate numerical sequences. The authors describe a divide between models that generate through superficial pattern matching and models that understand series but struggle to produce faithful numbers. Their approach uses an image-centered framework to bring the two capabilities into a common modeling process.

The first component, Bi-TSI, maps time series to images and images back to time series with near-lossless fidelity. Preserving numerical information through both directions matters because the visual representation must support accurate output as well as interpretation. The second component uses calibrated chain-of-thought reasoning to make understanding an explicit control signal for generation.

The authors also introduce TSUMM-Suite, pairing six time-series understanding tasks with two generation tasks. Their experiments report significant improvements in semantic understanding and numerical precision. These findings support the proposed combination of faithful representation conversion and understanding-guided generation. The framework connects the model's interpretation of a series to the numerical content it subsequently produces.
icml-2026-timeomni-vl-unified-models-for.tldr: TimeOmni-VL uses near-lossless image mappings and understanding-guided reasoning to unify time-series interpretation with accurate numerical generation.

paragraphs: TritonGym evaluates language-model workflows for generating Triton GPU kernels. The authors argue that existing evaluations place too much emphasis on a model's first code attempt and too little on tool use and feedback. That leaves an incomplete picture of agents whose performance depends on the sequence of actions they take while developing code.

The benchmark supplies a shared orchestration framework and standardized function-call access to code-generation tools. This common interface is designed to distinguish model capability from the contribution of workflow design. It gives researchers a more consistent basis for comparing different ways of organizing GPU coding agents and their interactions with tools.

Its task coverage includes a maintained operator set, community samples, out-of-distribution tasks, and domain-specific language extensions. These categories support both breadth and extensibility as coding requirements change. The contribution is evaluation infrastructure for studying agentic GPU programming, with the stated aim of making development more accessible and supporting practical adoption. The abstract emphasizes the framework's scope and purpose rather than reporting a performance ranking.
icml-2026-tritongym-a-benchmark-for-agen.tldr: TritonGym standardizes tools, tasks, and orchestration for comparing agentic workflows that generate Triton GPU kernels.

paragraphs: VENOMREC studies a poisoning threat to recommendation systems built on multimodal language models. Agreement between modalities can often reduce the effect of conventional attacks that alter interaction logs or only one modality. The authors find that coordinated manipulation across modalities creates a different vulnerability: poisoned inputs can steer fused representations in stable semantic directions during fine-tuning.

The paper formalizes this cross-modal interactive poisoning setting and introduces an attack with two components. Exposure Alignment identifies high-exposure regions in the shared embedding space. Cross-modal Interactive Perturbation then creates coupled text-token and image-patch edits guided by attention. The mechanism exploits the interaction between modalities within the learned recommendation representation.

Experiments on four real-world multimodal datasets report a mean ER@20 of 0.73, averaging 0.52 absolute ER points above the strongest baseline while retaining comparable recommendation utility. The findings show that ordinary recommendation quality can remain similar while targeted promotion becomes more effective. They identify synchronized multimodal poisoning as a distinct threat to systems that rely on cross-modal agreement.
icml-2026-venomrec-cross-modal-interacti.tldr: VENOMREC shows that coordinated text-and-image poisoning can promote targeted items in multimodal recommenders while maintaining comparable recommendation utility.

paragraphs: This paper introduces forecasting under hypothetical future conditions expressed in text. Historical patterns alone may not describe what happens when forthcoming events change the situation. The authors argue that methods centered on factual conditions or simple structured inputs do not adequately capture the complexity of these scenarios. Text provides a more flexible way to specify the conditions a forecast should reflect.

The task creates an evaluation challenge because a hypothetical scenario may have no observed future series to compare against. The authors propose an evaluation framework covering both factual and counterfactual settings, including cases without ground-truth time series. This makes evaluation part of the contribution alongside the forecasting task itself.

Their forecasting mechanism attributes information in the text to mutable and immutable factors. That distinction helps determine which aspects should respond to the scenario and which should remain stable. The abstract reports improved accuracy under sophisticated, stochastic textual conditions. The contribution links flexible scenario descriptions, structured treatment of their effects, and evaluation when direct counterfactual observations are unavailable.
icml-2026-what-if-tomorrow-is-the-world-.tldr: The paper introduces text-conditioned counterfactual forecasting, with evaluation for unobserved scenarios and a mechanism separating mutable from immutable factors.
